text: The comedy to horror pipeline is interesting. Jordan Peele went from comedy sketches on MadTV and Key & Peele to Get Out, Us, and Nope. Danny McBride went from absurd comedies to writing the most recent Halloween trilogy. The director of the Halloween trilogy, David Gordon Green, also did comedies, including Pineapple Express (which starred Danny McBride), but he was arguably from a more serious background before that. Curry Barker went from YouTube comedy sketches to writing and directing Obsession. Zach Cregger did internet sketch comedy with The Whitest Kids U Know and went onto writing and directing the horror movies Barbarian and Weapons. text: Watched Obsession. This is the most terrifying film I have ever seen. It's gory, but not as gory as The Furious; That's not the point. It is deeply psychological and bathes in anxiety, guilt and tension ten times more than in bodily fluids. - brilliant writing - absolutely outstanding acting - visual design, sound design, cinematography, top notch Some things would be over the top in isolation, but in context they're exactly right. This movie is very intense. Cowardice, selfishness, the nature of love, actions and consequences, responsibility, boundaries, social dynamics ... apart from my body shaking with tension, my head was spinning the entire time with the moral dilemmas and the frustration with the situations. This was an amazing film. I'm glad I saw it and I'm glad I saw it in the cinema. I will not be seeing it again for a looong time. #obsession #ObsessionFilm #CurryBarker #IndeNavarrette
